messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Malayalam, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Ahi | Interjection expressing emotional intensity | Render as Malayalam exclamation **“അയ്യോ!”** (ayyō) — *Back‑translation: Ah!* | | quanto | Degree adverb intensifying “hard” (scalar, not comparative) | Use a high‑intensity degree marker **“എത്ര”** (eṟṟa) before the adjective; specify **positive‑intensity** (no >/< relation) — *Back‑translation: how* | | a | Preposition introducing infinitival complement “to tell” | Translate with infinitival marker **“ക്ക്”** (kku) attached to the verb — *Back‑translation: to* | | dir | Infinitive verb “to tell” | Use Malayalam infinitive **“പറയാന്‍”** (paṟaṇ) with appropriate case marking from the preceding preposition — *Back‑translation: tell* | | qual | Interrogative/relative pronoun “what” introducing content clause | Render as **“എന്ത്”** (eṉt) introducing the embedded question — *Back‑translation: what* | | era | Imperfect past of “to be” (3 sg.) | Use past tense copula **“ആയിരുന്നു”** (āyirunnu) with 3rd‑person singular agreement — *Back‑translation: was* | | è | Present copula (3 sg.) | Use present copula **“ആണ്”** (āṇ) with 3rd‑person singular agreement — *Back‑translation: is* | | cosa | Noun “thing” (abstract) | Translate as **“വസ്തു”** (vasthu) in nominative case — *Back‑translation: thing* | | dura | Predicate adjective “hard” (feminine singular) | Use adjective **“കഠിനം”** (kaṭhinaṁ) agreeing with “thing” (neuter in Malayalam) — *Back‑translation: hard* | | esta | Demonstrative adjective “this” (archaic) | Render as **“ഈ”** (ī) preceding the noun — *Back‑translation: this* | | selva | Noun “wood/forest” (feminine singular) | Translate as **“കാട്”** (kāṭ) in nominative case — *Back‑translation: wood* | | selvaggia | Attributive adjective “wild” | Use **“കാട്ടു”** (kāṭṭu) as pre‑nominal modifier — *Back‑translation: wild* | | e (1) | Coordinating conjunction “and” | Render as **“മറ്റ്”** (maṭṭ) linking adjectives — *Back‑translation: and* | | aspra | Attributive adjective “rough” | Use **“മുറുകിയ”** (muṟukiya) as pre‑nominal modifier — *Back‑translation: rough* | | e (2) | Coordinating conjunction “and” | Same as above **“മറ്റ്”** (maṭṭ) — *Back‑translation: and* | | forte | Attributive adjective “dense/strong” | Use **“കട്ടിയുള്ള”** (kaṭṭiyuḷḷa) as pre‑nominal modifier — *Back‑translation: dense* | | che | Relative pronoun “which” | Render as **“അത്”** (atu) followed by a relative clause marker **“‑യുള്ള”** (‑yulla) — *Back‑translation: which* | | nel | Contraction “in the” (preposition + definite article) | Translate as **“ചിന്തയില്‍”** (cintayil) where **“‑യില്‍”** (‑yil) marks locative “in” — *Back‑translation: in* | | pensier | Noun “thought” (poetic form) | Use **“ചിന്ത”** (cinta) in locative case (‑യില്‍) — *Back‑translation: thought* | | rinova | Present verb “renews” (3 sg.) | Use present progressive **“പുതുക്കുന്നു”** (puthukkunna) with 3rd‑person singular agreement — *Back‑translation: renews* | | la | Definite article (feminine) – marks “the” | Malayalam lacks articles; ensure the noun **“ഭയം”** (bhayam) is definite by context — *Back‑translation: the* | | paura | Noun “fear” (feminine singular) | Translate as **“ഭയം”** (bhayam) in accusative case (same as nominative) — *Back‑translation: fear* |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Malayalam components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 4: അയ്യോ എത്ര പറയാന്‍ എന്തായിരുന്നു വസ്തു കഠിനമാണ് / അയ്യോ എന്തായിരുന്നു വസ്തു എന്ന് പറയാന്‍ എത്ര കഠിനമാണ് / അയ്യോ പറയാന്‍ എന്തായിരുന്നു വസ്തു എത്ര കഠിനമാണ് - Line 5: ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റു മുറുകിയ മറ്റു കട്ടിയുള്ള / ഈ കാട്ടു മറ്റു മുറുകിയ മറ്റു കട്ടിയുള്ള കാട് / ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റു മുറുകിയ മറ്റു കട്ടിയുള്ള - Line 6: അത് ചിന്തയില്‍ പുതുക്കുന്നു ഭയം / അത് ചിന്തയില്‍ ഭയം പുതുക്കുന്നു / അത് ചിന്തയില്‍ പുതുക്കുന്ന ഭയം

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Malayalam lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura
**Line Inventory:** - അയ്യോ എന്തായിരുന്നു വസ്തു എന്ന് പറയാന്‍ എത്ര കഠിനമാണ്
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already contains the exclamation, degree marker, infinitival complement, content clause and the predicate “hard”.
**Target Text:** അയ്യോ എന്തായിരുന്നു വസ്തു എന്ന് പറയാന്‍ എത്ര കഠിനമാണ്
---
**Source Line:** 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte
**Line Inventory:** - ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റു മുറുകിയ മറ്റു കട്ടിയുള്ള
**Assembly Notes:** - Inserted the coordinating conjunction **മറ്റ്** (function word) between the three adjectives to link them as “wild and rough and dense”.
**Target Text:** ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റു മുറുകിയ മറ്റു കട്ടിയുള്ള
---
**Source Line:** 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura!
**Line Inventory:** - അത് ചിന്തയില്‍ ഭയം പുതുക്കുന്നു
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra morphology required; the phrase expresses the relative clause “which in thought renews the fear”.
**Target Text:** അത് ചിന്തയില്‍ ഭയം പുതുക്കുന്നു!

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Malayalam text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 4 - Target Text (from Step 4): അയ്യോ എന്തായിരുന്നു വസ്തു എന്ന് പറയാന്‍ എത്ര കഠിനമാണ് - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): Ah! what was thing that to tell how hard is - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what … - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 5 - Target Text (from Step 4): ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റു മുറുകിയ മറ്റു കട്ടിയുള്ള - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): this wood wild and rough and dense - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): this wild and rough and dense wood … - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 6 - Target Text (from Step 4): അത് ചിന്തയില്‍ ഭയം പുതുക്കുന്നു! - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): that in thought fear renews! - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): which in thought renews the fear! - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
```malayalam അയ്യോ എന്തായിരുന്നു വസ്തു എന്ന് പറയാന്‍ എത്ര കഠിനമാണ് ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റു മുറുകിയ മറ്റു കട്ടിയുള്ള അത് ചിന്തയില്‍ ഭയം പുതുക്കുന്നു! ```
